chunks: From him, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Thabit ibn Sharih, from Dawud al-Abzari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"It is not valid that you lend a fruit (crop) and take a better one from it in another land, other than what you lent from it."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on lending crops and taking better quality in return?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of *Qard al-Thamarah* (loan of crops), prohibiting the exchange of a specific loaned quantity for a superior or different quality in another location, thereby preventing hidden usury (*Riba*) in agricultural transactions. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on strict equality in kind and quality to ensure fairness in deferred agricultural exchanges, a principle vital for pre-harvest financing in early Islamic societies.
